A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same SH-Bench/BPFT study, and their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison. V1's reference to an absent split-results table is an identifiable document omission that v3 addresses.

before.justification: V1 reports original SH-Bench evaluations, BPFT fine-tuning results, and speaker-description, refusal and open-ended-question experiments in Tables 2–5.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports numerical real-versus-synthetic breakdowns and confidence intervals in its appendix.

M1.justification: BPFT retains the same paired general/selective training instructions and LoRA fine-tuning of the Qwen-2.5-Omni 7B and Step-Audio-2-mini language backbones, with rank 32 and other components frozen. Terminology and explanatory edits introduce no procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 3,968 audio files, five real-world scenarios, AMI-derived synthetic audio, and MCQ/open-ended tasks. The demographic disclosure and partition scores in v3 do not establish expanded populations or task coverage.

E2.justification: The pipeline, five open-source configurations, Gemini 2.5 Pro and GPT-4o-audio-preview remain the same comparators in Table 2. Comparator membership in Tables 3–5 also remains unchanged; the new split table reports existing systems.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, sample counts, audio-mixing settings, model configurations, evaluation modes and metrics remain unchanged. The prompts moved from Appendix A.1 to A.4 are identical. The added Wilson intervals change uncertainty reporting rather than the evaluation design.

E4.justification: The existing real-versus-synthetic analysis gains numerical support through Table 6, allowing inspection of the discussed differences in comprehension and privacy protection across partitions. The speaker-description, IDK-removal/entropy and open-ended refusal analyses in Tables 3–5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without statistical intervals. V3 introduces systematic 95% Wilson score confidence intervals for all four main accuracy measures across every system in Table 8, with methodological discussion in Appendix A.3. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting without reporting additional runs or seeds.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 remain unchanged. V3 supplies previously absent partition scores in Table 6 and corrects the prose's unfine-tuned bystander-comprehension leader from Gemini (65.5%) to Kimi (67.4%). Some new split scores are inconsistent with retained aggregates: Qwen+BPFT's selective bystander scores of 90.0%/99.6% average to 94.8%, versus 93.8% in Table 2.

T1.justification: Selective Efficacy remains the same harmonic mean of four accuracies in Equation 1. No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are substantively revised; the Wilson-interval addition concerns statistical reporting.

C1.justification: The core SH-Bench, SE and BPFT contributions remain intact. V3 adds a headline claim of an absolute 47-percentage-point selective bystander accuracy advantage over Gemini in the abstract and contribution list. Table 2 supports only 36.9 points: 96.1% versus 59.2%.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the new confidence intervals as evidence that improvements are unlikely to reflect sampling variation. It also expands discussion of BPFT's differing effects on main-speaker accuracy for Qwen and Step-Audio, and explains the distance-based motivation for bystander attenuation. The stated applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds speaker demographics and instructions for identifying AMI demographics, specifies smartphone/laptop recording devices, clarifies substantive-speech segment selection, and supplies the ethics approval number. It removes v1's direct dataset link while retaining the equivalent code-repository link; this establishes a documentation change, not changed resource availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds MSU-Bench (Wang et al., 2025b) and Zhan et al. (2024), acknowledging prior bystander-privacy work in multimodal LLMs while preserving the claimed gap in systematic audio-LLM benchmarking and mitigation. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata or remove duplication.

P1.justification: V3 replaces LALMs with audio LLMs, edits prose across the abstract, introduction, related work and results, and updates author information. The main section sequence remains intact; the appendix expands to four subsections, relocating the unchanged prompts from A.1 to A.4.

P2.justification: V3 adds appendix tables for partition scores, demographics and confidence intervals; the interval table redisplays the main results with added uncertainty information. Existing figures and main tables are retained, with limited label, caption, sizing and page-flow adjustments.

improvement.justification: V3 improves auditability by supplying the missing partition table, adding confidence intervals and correcting the Kimi/Gemini ranking. However, it introduces a prominent 47-point advantage claim where Table 2 supports 36.9 points, and its new Qwen+BPFT partition scores imply 94.8% rather than the retained 93.8% aggregate. These useful reporting additions coexist with material new numerical inconsistencies, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
